thread:
Maria Chen: quick idea — can we add a ‘compact exposure’ toggle on the SLO card that shows estimated notify volume and a noise score preview? links: https://app.prototype/redwood/exposure (mock)
Diego Alvarez: do you mean per-route? how do we estimate notify volume without reprocessing all signals? :thinking:
Maria Chen: per-route + per-tenant preview. use recent sample windows + fanout model. not exact but useful for UX before committing thresholds.
Priya Nair: +1. show both sampled-estimate and worst-case (full fanout) numbers. also surface cost delta if we change quieting or threshold.
Tom Becker: API-wise this implies a new preview endpoint or expanding /routes/:id/preview. prefer a dedicated /routes/:id/slo_exposure_preview to keep contracts clear.
Tom Becker: proposal (very small):
```
GET /routes/:id/slo_exposure_preview?window=30d&tier=all
response: {"sampled_estimate": 412, "worst_case_estimate": 2890, "noise_score": 0.72}
```
Diego Alvarez: how do we compute noise_score? telemetry team has a classifier but it's heavy.
Riley (telemetry): we can reuse the offline classifier but run it on a sampled batch (1-2% of recent events) and extrapolate. need to expose sampling params in the preview request.
Priya Nair: UX: show ‘sample size’ and a confidence band. users should know it's approximate. maybe a little info tooltip.
Maria Chen: yes — tooltip: "Preview based on sampled events; actual alerts may vary. Use rollout to validate." :information_source:
Tom Becker: real question: do we store preview results or compute on demand? storing requires retention and privacy considerations for private deploys.
Riley (telemetry): compute-on-demand is fine for hosted. for Private/VPC customers we should default to disabled and let SEs opt-in. compute cost should be bounded by sampling.
Diego Alvarez: routing implications: if preview suggests high fanout we should offer one-click mitigations: increase quiet-window, escalate-only rules, or suggest per-entity rate limits.
Priya Nair: add suggested mitigations UI + quick apply button that generates a canary rollout (e.g., 10% tenants) — so users can test without global changes.
Tom Becker: canary API sketch:
```
POST /routes/:id/rollouts
body: {"type":"slo_quieting_canary","percent":10,"changes":{"quiet_window":60}}
```
Maria Chen: rollout UX: show telemetry baseline, expected notify reduction, and backfill metrics after canary completes.
Diego Alvarez: alerting team: pls confirm if notify-estimates should include third-party integrations (pagerduty/slack) — those have different fanout semantics.
Riley (telemetry): include integration multipliers in worst-case estimate, but keep sampled_estimate as internal-delivery only. show both.
Priya Nair: accessibility: compact view should collapse details but allow expand for full estimate breakdown.
Maria Chen: rollout plan: start with internal alpha on prod for eng teams, then opt-in for a few friendly tenants, then global by feature-flag. default off for tenants >5000 alerts/day.
Tom Becker: sounds good. I'll draft the API RFC with privacy notes and estimated compute cost.
Diego Alvarez: I'll add UI mocks and the suggested mitigation flows.
Riley (telemetry): I'll prototype the sampled pipeline and return a simple noise_score + confidence.
Priya Nair: I'll wire up the quick-apply canary flow in the console mock and add tooltip copy.
Maria Chen: great — action items: Tom (RFC), Diego (mock), Riley (sampling POC), Priya (UI + copy). meet Friday standup to sync? :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: slo-exposure-preview-feature-flag -> staging at 2024-11-06T14:00:00Z :rocket:
Maria Chen: perfect, thanks everyone :eyes:
Priya Nair: thanks!
Tom Becker: thanks — I'll ping when RFC is ready.
Diego Alvarez: done for now.
Riley (telemetry): noted. will post perf numbers soon.
